title and abstract.summary: The study measured the effect of near-to-nature management strategies on the functional diversity of saproxylic beetle species across various European forest types, using both continental and regional data. The study evaluated the effect of nearly natural management strategies on the functional diversity of saproxylic beetles by relating their functional traits to ecosystem characteristics across 8 European countries and a large forest in southern Germany. introduction.summary: The study investigated the effects of forest-use intensity on the occurrence of saproxylic beetle species and the composition of their assemblages with respect to their traits (body size and habitat niche positions).

results.summary: The study measured the composition and associated traits (such as diameter and decay niches) of saproxylic beetle assemblages across two datasets: a European-wide data set and a regional data set. The measurements covered many species, totaling 709 species in the European data set and 284 species in the regional data set.
